matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value, then compute the numeric difference between the two sides. This guides which value changes are needed to achieve equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start, before enumerating stick moves, to know the target adjustment.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the computed difference and proposing a move that does not address the numeric gap.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be relocated from any character to any other character, ensuring both source and destination remain valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the needed numeric change, generate all candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Considering a move that leaves the source character with no sticks, making it an invalid symbol.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the numeric values of the affected numerals change and check whether the net change equals the required discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Accepting a move that changes the left side by +3 when the discrepancy is +5.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat the '=' sign as two horizontal sticks; moving one of them can turn it into a '-' while the remaining stick stays a minus sign (or keep '=' if enough sticks remain).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the needed numeric adjustment can be achieved by changing the operator sign.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '=' and assuming the operator remains '=', resulting in an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick turns it into a '-' while the horizontal stick can be used elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and a vertical stick can be repurposed to adjust a numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' and leaving a stray horizontal stick unattached, breaking the operator.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be transferred directly from one operator to another, simultaneously altering both operators while preserving exactly one '=' sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy can be resolved by swapping or changing operator signs.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '-' to '+' but forgetting to update both operators, leaving one malformed.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral would increase (or decrease) its value by the needed amount, consider moving a stick from an operator (e.g., '=', '-') to that numeral, ensuring the operator remains a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the required numeric change matches a known single‑stick numeral transformation.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '=' to a numeral but leaving '=' with no sticks, eliminating the equality sign.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=', and each side must have at least one valid numeral; operators must remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any proposed transformation, before final acceptance.
matchstick.example: Dropping the '=' sign entirely when moving its stick, so the equation no longer has an equality.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Map common single‑stick changes (X↔V, I↔V, I↔X) to their numeric value changes (±5, ±4, ±9) and use this map to quickly assess candidate moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating a stick move that alters a numeral, refer to this map to compute the numeric impact.
matchstick.example: Assuming moving a stick from V to I changes V to I (+/-4) without checking that the resulting shape is valid.

matchstick.title: Identical numerals operator conversion
matchstick.principle: If both sides already contain the same numeral, moving a stick from the '+' operator to turn it into '-' (or vice‑versa) can balance the equation without changing numeral values.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains identical numerals on both sides and the discrepancy is zero after operator change.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' but forgetting to re‑evaluate the arithmetic, leaving the equality false.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character that leaves it with an impossible shape (e.g., a single diagonal stick) which is not a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed move, verify that both the source and destination characters still correspond to a recognized numeral or operator.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model proposes a move but does not recompute the equation's numeric values, leading to a final equation that is still false.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recalculate the integer values of both sides after applying a stick move and confirm they are equal before output.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the output, the model truncates or removes characters (e.g., missing the right‑hand side), producing an incomplete equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final answer reproduces the full equation with all numerals and operators, only altering characters via the single stick move.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: When an operator is altered (e.g., '-' to '+'), the model forgets that this changes the arithmetic result, leading to a mismatch.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When changing an operator, recompute the expression using the new operator and verify equality.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model either moves no stick or moves more than one, violating the puzzle constraint.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Explicitly track that exactly one stick is relocated: one source loses a stick, one destination gains a stick, and no other changes occur.
